1.why: All screens use a clean bold sans-serif with roomy line height and clear label/field spacing, though no explicitly dyslexia-friendly face is evidenced.

2.why: No italics or all-caps are used and every instruction is a single short sentence rather than a paragraph block.

3.why: The single-column card layout and large tap-target button suggest mobile suitability, but only ~1280px desktop captures are provided so mobile rendering is unverified.

4.why: Instructions such as 'Sign in to begin. Take your time.' and 'Enter the same contact details again.' are short and in plain language.

5.why: Placeholders ('name@example.com', '07123 456789') plus explicit 'Demo:' hints show exactly what input is expected.

6.why: Every step presents only one-line helper texts; no long passage must be read to continue.

7.why: No copy-to-clipboard control appears anywhere; the flow dies at step 2 so no secret or backup code is ever presented to copy.

8.why: No QR code or scan alternative is shown in any screenshot, as authenticator provisioning never renders.

9.why: Standard email/phone/password inputs exist but nothing in the screenshots evidences autocomplete support, and 'Demo:' credential hints imply manual typing.

10.why: A 'Step X of 6' label, progress bar, and single filled blue primary button make the current step and main action visually prominent.

11.why: Each screen asks for one grouped task with a single primary button, though the login screen combines three fields in one submission.

12.why: Step 2 confirms plainly ('You are signed in. Next, confirm your identity.'), but after confirming identity the system only outputs the raw 'Invalid array length' and states nothing about what happened or comes next.

13.why: Hints promise 'You can correct and retry these details', but the flow is hard-blocked at step 2 and no reveal/hide or re-request of codes exists since codes are never generated.

14.why: 'Invalid array length' is a raw technical exception that names neither the actual problem nor any fix.

15.why: The interface explicitly states 'No reading timer. You can retry any step.' and 'Take your time', with no countdown visible anywhere.
